rule: Minotaur levels: a timer created on the player-start entity counts ticks. At arrival minus 30 s one roll (1 in 5, one tick only) may summon a nine-human brigade at the timer point with a warning sound. At arrival time the minotaur is summoned once at the timer point with an arrival hint and sound; three seconds later a second hint and a sting play and the timer removes itself. Arrival is 150 s, or 210 s on listed depths. Level population: candidate cells (30 plus 0 to 9 by default, or header range), forced monsters from header bytes placed first, then forced loot and decorations; forced slots become an NPC at 1 in 10 after depth 1. Traps: min(clamp(depth,1,5) plus 0 to 4, free cells), halved on The Mines. Summon trap: proximity or signal trigger, interval in seconds times 50 ticks, count per cycle, cycles, failure percent; each summon paths to the trigger. Sleep: gnome 1 in 8, imp 1 in 4, unless spawn is flagged no-sleep. Formation: leader update at most once per second; wedge slots. Known defect: brigade leader id is declared inside the loop so the group never links.
keep: Visible countdown with a one-in-N warning and a single arrival beat at the level entrance
Traps announced by sound at two distances (far and near text tiers)
Summon trap cadence: trigger, interval, count per cycle, cycles, failure percent
Sleepers on spawn with a roll and a tick duration
Mimic inert until touched, then path to the toucher
Wedge formation for followers (fits three attack slots)
change: Nine-human brigade becomes three attack slots plus a queue (MAX_ATTACKERS = 3)
Brigade leader linkage fixed (declare the leader id before the loop)
Warning becomes a one-second window with a latched warned flag, rolled once
Summon trap random pool becomes a per-zone list
Monster table by map name moves from code switch (maps.cpp biome branches) to zone data
Sleep duration unit stated in the data row (ticks assumed, decrement not read)
Shape, names, sounds and boss silhouette changed; not copied
look_test: Build a 150 s pursuit clock in one test zone with a corner countdown ring. At 120 s a one-in-five roll decides whether three tokens appear at the zone entrance with a warning sound. At 150 s one creature enters from the entrance, then a second line and a sting follow three seconds later. Compare always-warn against one-in-five on a 375-wide phone and judge whether the entrance arrival reads as a threat and whether the warning reads as a choice.
